authority: NONE — DERIVED TRUTH. Measurement of tracked repository state.
determinism: No wall clock, no commit identity, no working-tree status. The bytes are a pure function of tracked content, so two runs over one tree are byte-identical.

ratchet.justification: The two are engine/__init__.py (2 statements) and platform/__init__.py (15 statements, 4 imports). Both are ROOT package initialisers of trees measured per SUB-package, and that shape is what puts them outside every rule: coverage sources name engine.foundation and platform.identity, never engine or platform, so no source covers the initialiser itself. Naming the roots instead would admit engine.uicm — 1,893 statements with zero test files, declared exempt with a written reason — and convert a dead-code finding into a coverage figure, which is the measurement laundering the exemption register exists to prevent. Ω FOUND THESE: both were absent from coverage.xml under the enumerated denominator and no control could say so. WHAT CLOSES THIS FLOOR: retiring or testing engine.uicm, after which the roots can be measured whole and this metric reaches 0. That is an owner decision about dead code, not a coverage setting.
ratchet.subject: artifacts no Ω-5 rule could explain (Ω-C-07). The bucket that must empty.

ratchet.justification: Artifacts whose top-level root is not a Python identifier — 00-MASTER, 00-BOOK and 00-CMG — so NO coverage source could name them, by the language's own rule for identifiers rather than by any policy here. They are governance engines: owned (Ω-2 derives an authority for every one), invoked (verify.sh stages, Makefile targets and workflows all reach them) and unmeasurable by coverage as currently laid out. WHAT CLOSES THIS FLOOR: making those engines importable under test rather than only executable as scripts, which is a real change to how they are structured and not a setting. Until then the population may fall and hold; it may never rise, because a floor accepts the stall and never a regression.
